releaseNotes: Added knowledge/engineering/technical-documentation-ste100.md: this repo's technical documentation (architecture docs, engineering specs, ADRs, runbooks, API/config references, this skill's own knowledge/*.md files) now follows Simplified Technical English (ASD-STE100) -- flat, literal, one-meaning-per-word -- instead of no-slop-writing.md's voice-preserving rules. Wired via a new domain.engineering catalog reference (reference.engineering.technical-documentation-ste100) so the loadWhen graph pulls it in automatically. Placement resolved via llm-council: excludes root README.md/AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md, which stay with no-slop-writing.md's existing check:no-slop gate, and defers engine-generated business-repo docs to a later, separately scoped change. Cross-linked from no-slop-writing.md section 8. Reference-only for now; a mechanical gate extension is a logged follow-up, not built in this change.
Added a one-line 'Documentation style' pointer to root AGENTS.md so the repo-wide policy has a home before any catalog-graph discovery happens.

PR review (Codex) caught two real gaps, both fixed. First: the reference's trigger line named engineering/TECH_SPEC.md, engineering/ENGINEERING_PLAN.md, and engineering/PRODUCTION_READINESS.md as governed files, but every file with those three names in this repository is actually a workspace/business/engineering/ or workspace-template/ generated-business template -- the exact surface the same file's §2 excludes. Reworded the trigger and §2 to name a maintainer-authored spec instead, with the exclusion stated by path. Second, and larger: the standard was reference-only, so catalog/audit checks passed even if a governed document violated every rule -- 'always uses ASD-STE100' was not enforceable. Resolved via llm-council (First Principles' framing won 3/3 in anonymous peer review): built check:documentation-ste100 (validation/business/engineering/check-technical-docs-ste100.ts), a mechanical two-rule subset -- sentence length and a present-perfect heuristic -- at two severity tiers mirroring check-no-slop.ts's own front-door split. Error tier applies today to the one file this change can guarantee compliant (the reference itself, which the new checker caught failing its own 20-word rule 13 times on first run -- real signal, not a rubber stamp -- and was rewritten into short sentences and bullet lists until it passed clean). Warning tier applies repo-wide to the rest of the governed knowledge/**/*.md surface (excluding knowledge/words/, which keeps no-slop-writing.md's register), giving real, non-blocking signal on pre-existing prose. Five fail-then-catch fixture cases in repo-gates.fixtures.ts prove the checker fires on both rules and respects the tier split, not just that it passes. Two peer-review-caught parser bugs fixed live: markdown bullet items were merging into one oversized sentence (list items now force their own boundary), and a colon-introduced clause or list now also ends a sentence chunk.

A second Codex review round on the same file caught two more real gaps, both fixed. First: the reference's own trigger line names this skill's own README.md and SKILL.md as governed, but the checker's file discovery never enqueued either one -- an edit to either received no signal at all. Added both, relative to --skill-root so the fix stays root-agnostic. Second: a trailing prose paragraph with no terminal punctuation (no `.`/`!`/`?`/`:` before end of file) fell off the end of the sentence-matching regex entirely, so an oversized or present-perfect closing sentence passed silently as long as the file just stopped instead of ending in punctuation. Fixed by forcing a boundary at the end of the joined text when one is not already present. Two new fail-then-catch fixtures prove both fixes: one confirms README.md now gets scanned, one confirms a violation in an unterminated final sentence is still caught.

A third Codex review round caught two more real gaps, both fixed. First: docs/platform/technical-architecture.md and docs/platform/product-architecture.md -- current, real architecture docs -- were outside the checker's hardcoded docs/ list, so an edit to either got no signal despite the repo policy governing architecture docs. Added both paths explicitly (a full dynamic docs/ scan was considered and rejected: docs/brainstorms/, docs/plans/, and point-in-time historical audits under docs/platform/ are deliberately exploratory or frozen-record prose this repo's own conventions already keep outside every gate, so a blanket scan would pull in files that were never meant to be governed). Second, and more serious: the prior round's 'colon also ends a chunk' fix (added to stop a bullet-list intro from merging into its first item) was a real regression -- it let a single long grammatical sentence with a mid-sentence colon (`Follow this procedure: open the file, ...`) escape the 20-word ceiling by splitting into two short-looking halves that each passed individually. Replaced the blanket colon rule with a narrow, structural one: a line ending in ':' converts to a real boundary only when the very next line is a list item, so a list-introducing colon still gets its boundary while an ordinary colon-joined sentence stays one sentence for counting purposes. Three new fail-then-catch fixtures prove this: a mid-sentence-colon instruction over the ceiling is caught, the same construction under the ceiling still passes, and the narrow exception is proven narrow (no false boundary when no list follows).

A fourth Codex review round caught two more real gaps, both fixed -- the second time in a row a hardcoded path list missed a currently-existing governed file, so the discovery mechanism itself was the real problem, not the missing entry. First: validation/repository/source-freshness-maintenance.md, an active maintenance runbook the reference's own scope names ('a runbook'), was outside every discovery path (not under docs/ or knowledge/). Replaced the ad hoc per-round path patching with an explicit, extensible ADDITIONAL_GOVERNED_DIRECTORIES list (validation/repository/, tooling/) walked the same way as knowledge/ -- adding a future runbook location is now a one-line array edit, not a new bespoke code block. Second: markdown table rows were dropped outright rather than scanned, so an unquoted present-perfect sentence hiding in a table cell got no signal at all -- demonstrated by the reference's own §3 rule table, which already contains a present-perfect example ('The validator has read the file.') as an intentional 'Don't' illustration. Fixed by scanning table cells as discrete units (same forced-boundary treatment as list items) while stripping double-quoted spans from all prose first, so a cited or illustrative example in quotes -- exactly what the §3 table's Do/Don't columns are -- is read as data being discussed, not the document's own assertion. Three new fail-then-catch fixtures prove this: the new runbook directory is scanned, an unquoted violation inside a table cell is caught, and the same violation stays exempt when quoted.

A fifth Codex review round caught three more real gaps, all fixed. First: run-audit.ts only echoed a passing step's full output under B2C_AUDIT_VERBOSE, a flag audit:ci never sets -- so the whole warning tier's 'real, non-blocking signal' promise was invisible in the one place CI actually reports results. Fixed at the shared orchestrator, not just this checker: every step's status line now carries a '(N warnings)' suffix parsed from the common reportAndExit summary, benefiting every two-tier validator repo-wide. Second: docs/platform/decisions-and-tradeoffs.md, an ADR as current and real as the two architecture docs already governed, was outside the hardcoded docs/ list. Added it explicitly, and left docs/platform/ as an explicit allowlist rather than a full directory scan on purpose -- documented inline -- since that directory also holds a historical audit, a founder-journey narrative, and an open backlog this repo's own conventions already keep outside every gate. Third, and most serious: the prior round's fix for table-cell quoted examples was a blanket double-quote strip applied to ALL prose, not just table cells -- so an ordinary quoted UI string or error message inside a real sentence lost its own violation along with its quote marks, anywhere in the governed surface, not only in tables. Replaced the blanket strip with a narrow, structural exemption: only a table cell whose entire trimmed content is a single quoted string is dropped; a partial or embedded quote, in a table cell or plain prose, stays fully counted. Three new fail-then-catch fixtures prove this round: the ADR now gets scanned, a present-perfect phrase hidden inside a quoted UI string in plain prose is still caught, and a table cell with only a partial quote is still caught (while the whole-cell illustrative-example case from the prior round stays exempt).
